Sports.title: Gary Neville’s brutal one-word response to Mark Goldbridge question comes back to haunt him after buying YouTube channel
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE’S X post in which he rejected Mark Goldbridge coming on The Overlap has resurfaced.

It comes after Neville‘s The Overlap bought Goldbridge’s two YouTube channels.





The media company owned by Neville announced the news of the investment on Tuesday.

Goldbridge’s “That’s Football” and “The United Stand” were bought for a reported seven-figure-fee.

And since the purchase, fans have dug out an old post by Neville on X.

Three years ago one fan wrote: “Will Mark Goldbridge ever get invited onto The Overlap? The guy has the biggest MUFC fan channel and has a lot of football knowledge. It would be great to see him be brought on.”

The United legend and Sky Sports pundit, who founded The Overlap, swiftly shut down the question with an abrupt “no”.

So three years later after buying Goldbridge’s channels, Neville might have had a change of heart.

Goldbridge will continue to front both channels, which have a combined 3.7million subscribers.

However, they are set to be expanded as part of the takeover.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The United Stand will be expanded to include “Stick to United” as part of the “Stick to Football” podcast brand.

Journalists and former Man Utd players are expected to feature on the new show.

A new United news show named “The Daily United” will also be introduced.

Following the purchase Neville said: “We are building what we believe will become one of the most exciting independent football communities in the world – one that gives fans direct, personality-led content.



“The United Stand and That’s Football are two of the best-known football channels on YouTube, and our intention is to develop them into the most compelling Manchester United and football news channels in the market.”

Goldbridge added: “I’ve spent the last 10 years building The United Stand for Manchester United fans and That’s Football for all fans, and I’m prouder of that than anything I’ve ever done. This deal is about what comes next.

“The Overlap has the ambition, the credibility, and the resources to help me take what I do to the next level.”

Sports.title: Chelsea files: Blues face fresh fine, protesting fans’ damning blast at owners and Defoe’s scouting mission
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S defeat by Manchester City has added fuel to the fire of Saturday’s fan protest ahead of the Manchester United game.

The NotAProjectCFC group will lead the march with a simple message: BlueCo Out.





David and Jacob, leading figures at NAPCFC, told SunSport why the 3-0 beating by City was such a damning indictment of the Blues’ owners and their recruitment philosophy.

Former Chelsea Academy player Marc Guehi scored the second goal, after moving to the Etihad in January along with winger Antoine Semenyo.

Jacob said: “I think we can talk at length about how the club operate, but it was men against boys on Sunday.

“I think it was quite ironic that Marc Guehi scored a lovely goal at the Bridge and celebrated like it meant something big to him.



“That was a bit of a slap in the face.

“Can you imagine what Marc Guehi or Antoine Semenyo would probably have done to our team in January if the club had been prepared to put their hand in their pocket and pay people comparable salaries, rather than try and bring young talent in and lowball them and hope that they stay?”

Jacob and David discussed a number of issues, including Liam Rosenior’s appointment, which you can watch on YouTube.

The crux of their anger, though, is not merely Chelsea’s recruitment – it is the model as a whole.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They believe the identity of their club is being torn away from them, a feeling shared by some Strasbourg fans.

Supporters from BlueCo’s French club will join Saturday’s protest.

David added: “I think we are at a point now where we do not have any faith that this current ownership are the right people to take the club forward.

“When we first set up as a protest group around the turn of the year, just a few days before Enzo Maresca left the club,

“I think there was a feeling that we felt that with enough media pressure, we could perhaps put enough spotlight on the project itself and maybe look at a change to the model.



“Based on our communications with the club since, and based on our communications with people who probably better understand finances than we do, it doesn’t look like a realistic possibility.”

The last protest NAPCFC organised, ahead of the game against Brentford in January, was less impactful than they would have liked.

But it was still covered by plenty of media outlets, and it did prompt Chelsea director Danny Finkelstein to contact the group to arrange a meeting.

NAPCFC later revealed details of the encounter, including the claim Finkelstein told them it was “f***ing obvious” the Blues were building one of the best teams in the world.

Jacob and David feel they have planned much better and think Saturday’s event has the potential to be a huge turning point in Chelsea’s history.



David said: “For us the Brentford protest was a good way for us to work out how to structure these things going forward.

“The club reached out to the group, and we had everything that came from that.

“So there’s no doubt for us that it’s been part of something. But it’s about taking it on to the next level on Saturday.

“I think we’re approaching a point now where either you’re on one side or the other.

“It’s getting to the serious point of, if you do oppose protests, then you enable what Clearlake are doing and ripping the soul out of the club, and BlueCo ripping the soul out of the club, I should say.



“So this is an important moment. I think the image of us standing alongside Strasbourg will be powerful regardless of the overall number that are behind us.”

Jacob added: “David and I are not guys that are regularly out there on the picket line somewhere.

“It was something that we got involved in accidentally, and because we are passionate fans.

“I want my children to feel the same way about my football club as I did growing up. It was everything to me.



“These last four years have been really challenging from a football perspective.

“I should probably learn to detach the emotion from it, but it’s very difficult when you’ve loved the club for 30+ years, and been going to the stadium and having such nostalgic feelings.

“I don’t believe under this ownership, if we continue with this ownership, that we will have a football club that is representative of that.

“I’m not telling everyone, ‘this is our view, and it’s the right view.’ We believe that these aren’t the right people for the club. We want to do something about it.

“I think it’s evident with what we’ve seen over the last four years, and in particular, more recently, with the continuous churn of managers.



“They continuously try to control narratives…but there is no reality to it.

“I think it’s obvious that it is not working and that they do not have the best intentions for our football club. Look at the financial reports that have just come out.”

The protest will take place on Saturday, starting at the Wolfpack Inn at 6.30pm. Fans will march to Stamford Bridge for roughly 15 minutes ahead of the game against Manchester United.

SunSport will bring you complete coverage of that on our social media platforms and website.

FRIEND OR DEFOE?



Chelsea U21’s were defeated by Fulham in the final matchday of the Premier League 2 season, but still lifted the title.

At the game, though, was a familiar face for any Premier League fan – Jermain Defoe.

Defoe, now the manager of Woking FC, sat with the media and scouts at Fulham’s Motspur Park.

The former England striker would have been impressed by Shim Mheuka, who scored again for the young Blues, bringing his season total to 24 goals across all competitions

Mheuka will be out of reach for Woking.



But the young centre forward will be keen on a loan next season if he is unable to force his way into Chelsea’s first-team squad on a regular basis.

DISSENT DISASTER

Chelsea have received more yellow cards for dissent than any other team in the Premier League.

Perhaps a sign of the overall frustrations at Stamford Bridge, or the level of immaturity within the squad.



Chelsea have received 16 yellow cards for dissent in the Premier League, with both Estevao and Marc Cucurella receiving one each in Sunday’s defeat to Man City.

Vice-captain Enzo Fernandez has received four alone, more than any other player in the squad.

The Blues are achieving all this even without Nicolas Jackson, who is currently on loan at Bayern Munich.

Jackson infamously earned 10 bookings in his first season at the club, only one of them for a foul.

Yet the Senegal striker has received one yellow and one red card in 27 appearances for Bayern, while recording eight goals and four assists.



Jackson’s replacement, Liam Delap, has been booked twice and sent off once – for two yellow cards in seven minutes in the Carabao Cup tie at Wolves back in October.

Delap has two goals and four assists in his 34 appearances for the Blues.

FINE TIME

The Blues are facing yet another fine from the authorities.



The amount is trivial but the surrounding issues are not.

Chelsea Football Club Women Limited should have filed accounts for last season by the end of March at Companies House.

The financial penalty for a private company is £150 for being up to a month late, rising gradually to a maximum of £1,500 for over six months.

It is a bit of a mystery why full figures for the women’s team were not part of the information dump filed at CH earlier this week.

Owners BlueCo published their own results as well as those of the men’s team and other associated companies.



Within the BlueCo 22 Limited accounts, it was revealed CFC Women lost £17.1m in 2024-25 (up from £8.4m), despite turnover increasing by £9.8m as Sonia Bompastor’s side claimed a domestic Treble.

Eagle-eyed observers noticed something interesting in the figures for Chelsea FC Holdings, however.

The parent company of the men’s team received £22.6m from Chelsea Women last season – which was more than the women’s team’s total income of £21.3m.

It is believed the £22.6m includes the proceeds of selling the Kingsmeadow stadium to the women’s team.

And it also represents some kind of licensing agreement which allows the women’s team to exploit the Chelsea name and brand, as well as to benefit from services and facilities like Stamford Bridge that are controlled by Chelsea FC Holdings.



The latter’s accounts also revealed the company PAID out £11.3m to Chelsea Women over the course of last season.

But we won’t know for sure what the payments in either direction were for until the women’s team file their full figures at Companies House.

They will make interesting reading, not least for Aston Villa.

The owners of Villa have followed BlueCo in effectively selling their women’s team to themselves as a means of keeping the men’s team on the right side of the Premier League’s Profit and Sustainability Rules.

Chelsea would have breached PSR without the £198.7m profit from the sale of the women’s team in 2023-24.



SunSport understand the PL were aware of the Blues’ intention to charge the women’s team a licensing fee going forward.

And there has been no indication yet the PL is disputing the value of that agreement.

So expect Villa to follow their lead.

COMM OFF IT



Chelsea are sensitive about reporting of the increase in the executive wage bill last season.

And so they should be.

As SunSport revealed, the total cost of senior executives rose by nearly 80 per cent to £10.6m last season, despite the club making Premier League-record losses of £262.4m.

The club are at pains to point out the much bigger total was down to a significant increase in the number of staff classed as “key management personnel”, not huge pay rises for those who were already in that category.

But fans are still entitled to ask whether the Stamford Bridge suits who received £4.7m more between them last year are earning their keep.



Take the commercial department, for instance.

The Chelsea FC Holdings accounts revealed a fall in commercial income last season from £225.3m in the prior year to £200.9m, “largely due to reduced sponsorship revenue”.

In the summer, chief revenue officer Casper Stylsvig left the club after rows about the failure to find a new long-term front-of-shirt sponsor willing to meet the Blues’ valuation.

For the third season in a row, Chelsea began this campaign without such a deal, following the expiry of the agreement with mobile phone company 3 at the end of 2022-23 season.

Former Tottenham suit Todd Kline was promoted to president of commercial and in February the Blues announced a deal until the end of the season with Swedish AI firm IFS.



But not for the first time this season, claims there would soon be more good news on that front are are yet to be fulfilled.

And if Liam Rosenior’s team fail to qualify for the Champions League, the value of the shirt sponsorship and other deals will fall.

Chelsea ARE predicting club record revenues of around £700m this season.

But a lot of that increase will come from qualification for the Champions League and prize money from the Club World Cup – which were earned by the players, not the executives.

And there is still the issue of the progress – or lack of it – on a new stadium.



Building a modern, 60,000-seater ground is the single most important off-field task Chelsea chiefs face. Getting it right is probably the only way the current owners can increase the value of the asset on which they have already spent £4billion.

Yet nearly four years after the Clearlake Capital/Todd Boehly takeover, the club appears no nearer to resolving the problem.

WELCOME TO THE CHEAP SEATS

Chelsea’s clash with Manchester City last Sunday felt like a massive game that rich fans would love to watch.



But there were notably some empty seats in the West Stand opposite the press box.

And when you look at the prices the Blues are charging for Saturday’s big clash with Manchester United, you can see why.

At the time of going to press, there were still hospitality packages available in most categories.

They start at £595 plus VAT – in other words, more than £700 – for the right to see the game while paying for food and drink in areas away from the great unwashed.

And prices go right up to £7,495 plus VAT if you want to be in The Dugout Club.



For that, you get to greet the Chelsea team as they arrive, to watch the warm-up from the touchline, and to enjoy a post-match meet and greet with a player.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The package includes padded seats behind the home bench and swanky food and drink. Chelsea even throw in a matchday programme.

SunSport will have a think about it.

Sports.title: ‘There I was, crying’ – Liverpool icon left emotional in return to football as CEO of Malaysian club
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL legend Luis Garcia has admitted he was reduced to tears when his Malaysian club celebrated an historic win.

The former Spain midfielder retired from football in 2014 before a brief return to the game in 2016.





He has since worked as a pundit and didn’t think he would return to football.

But last summer he joined Malaysian side Johor Darul Ta’zim as their chief executive.

And Garcia has revealed he was left emotional after the team reached the quarter-finals of the Asian Champions League for the first team.

The club overcame Sanfrecce Hiroshima 3-2 on aggregate and will face Al-Ahli or Al-Duhail in the next round.

He told the Guardian: “I was always very competitive and once I had left football, I thought I wasn’t going to have those feelings I had before.

“I still enjoy football, still play seven-a-side with my friends – every Saturday at 10am, Los Jareños Club de Futbol – but I thought I had lost that and it wasn’t coming back.

“In fact, I was trying to avoid it; I didn’t want it. So when it happened, it surprised me. I didn’t expect football to give me that again. But there I was, crying.

“When I saw them jumping with joy, having been with them every day, sharing the long journeys, from Malaysia to Vietnam and back, on to Japan, and then saw them win I got that emotion again.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Garcia started his playing career with Barcelona and also had a spell with Atletico Madrid.

He moved to Liverpool in 2004 and enjoyed a Champions League triumph in his first season.

Garcia started as the Reds secured a dramatic penalty shootout win over AC Milan after coming back from 3-0 down.

He went on to win the FA Cup and Super Cup with Liverpool and reached another Champions League final in 2006-07.



Garcia played 122 times for Liverpool and then left Anfield as a cult iconm in 2007 to return to Atletico.

He later had stints with Racing Santander before playing in Mexico and India.

Garcia said a move into coaching never interested him after his retirement.

He claimed he was more attracted to the business side of football because he didn’t want “pressure without being able to impact the game”.

Garcia said: “When I retired, I was relaxed, welcomed the pause, but I had also spent years getting ready for other opportunities that might arise in football.



“I did a master’s with Uefa, a sporting director’s course, my coaching badges. Any qualification that was on the table, I took it.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But I didn’t want to coach. I always preferred the business side of it to the on-pitch stuff because I suffered a lot on the pitch.

“The idea of being a coach, being the other side of the line, all that pressure without being able to personally impact the game, didn’t appeal.”

Sports.title: Are Dream Team bosses overlooking dribble specialist Jeremy Doku ahead of Manchester City’s double header?
Sports.content:
TO say Dream Team managers are keen on Manchester City players this week is an understatement.

At the time of writing, the five most popular recruits for Gameweek 32 are: Rayan Cherki (£4.9m), March Guehi (£4.2m), Nico O’Reilly (£4.4m), Antoine Semenyo (£4.7m) and Erling Haaland (£6.6m).



Pep Guardiola’s side are scheduled to play twice this coming Gameweek.



This Sunday, they will host Arsenal in a highly anticipated match-up that many will believe will decide the Premier League title race.

Then on Wednesday night, City travel to Turf Moor to face Burnley, a league fixture rearranged to accommodate their FA Cup semi-final against Southampton (to follow in Gameweek 33).

This week’s popular strategy of recruiting Guardiola’s starters has a lot going for it.

But are Dream Team bosses overlooking Jeremy Doku (£4.3m) as an option?



The aforementioned transfer recruits are fully worthy of their popularity boosts (although O’Reilly is an injury doubt at this stage) but the Belgian winger might be a smart alternative for gaffers who need to think outside the box as the season nears its conclusion.

While Haaland, Semenyo and Guehi are the three most selected players in the game at present, Doku features in just 5.8% of teams.

That’s a low figure for somebody who has started City’s last four games and banked 26 points in the process.



The 23-year-old scored his side’s third goal at Stamford Bridge on Sunday, just his fourth of the season in all competitions.

However, the great thing about Doku in the realm of Dream Team is that he makes extensive use of other avenues to points.

He has registered 14 assists in 2025/26, a tally only bettered by Bruno Fernandes (£6.9m) and Cherki among all players.

Additionally, he ranks fourth overall for bonus points with 53 to his name.



There are no prizes for guessing how Doku earns his bonus points.

One of the best dribblers in world football, he has racked up 118 successful take-ons, putting him in a bracket of his own.

MOST SUCCESSFUL DRIBBLES THIS SEASON (ALL COMPS)

118 – Jeremy Doku

68 – Pedro Neto

65 – Hugo Ekitike

64 – Rayan Cherki

63 – Mohammed Kudus

60 – Yankuba Minteh

60 – Bukayo Saka

59 – Elliot Anderson

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Doku’s unmatched ability to bamboozle defenders has also helped him win 71 fouls having only given away 28 free-kicks in return — another surefire way to accumulate bonus points.

Gaffers are spoiled for choice when shopping around the Etihad this week and Doku deserves to be mentioned alongside the most tempting options.

Sports.title: History-making female manager hit with ‘embarassing’ and ‘insane’ sexist abuse after landing Bundesliga job
Sports.content:
UNION BERLIN’S latest manager Marie-Louise Eta has suffered abuse since becoming the first female to manage in the Bundesliga.

She was appointed on a deal until the end of the season at the weekend.





Union’s director of football Horst Heldt spoke out about the social media abuse the club’s latest appointment has suffered.

He said: “It’s just embarrassing. I’ve noticed it, but I also refuse to read or even just expose myself to that kind of nonsense because for me this is about quality – leadership quality.”

He added: “We have 100 per cent confidence in Loui – complete conviction. I find it insane that we have to deal with this in this day and age.

“We’re talking about a highly competent leader here, and you can be sure that everyone here at Union, whether in the stands or within the club itself, stands 100 per cent behind this decision and will do everything in their power to ensure that this doesn’t lead to any further discussion in the future.”

Eta, 34, made history by becoming the first female manager in Europe’s top five leagues.

She got the job following the sacking of Steffen Baumgart after a 3-1 defeat to Heidenheim.

The club sits 11th in the Bundesliga table but are still looking over their shoulders in the relegation battle.

Union Berlin are seven points clear of St Pauli in the relegation play-off spot of 16th.

Eta’s appointment as interim boss comes with her already being lined up as permanent head coach of the club’s women’s team in the summer.

It is not the first time Eta has made history – she became the first female assistant coach in Bundesliga history when she joined Union in 2023.

The following year she became the first woman to take charge of a men’s team in a Bundesliga game as head coach Nenad Bjelica served a three-match ban.

Eta’s first game in charge will come against relegation-threatened Wolfsburg on April 18 at the Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta gives Bukayo Saka injury update as Arsenal star battles Achilles problem ahead of Man City clash
Sports.content:
BUKAYO SAKA could return for Arsenal in “days not weeks”, says Mikel Arteta, amid fears over the winger’s condition.

The England star picked up an Achilles injury last month and hasn’t featured for the Gunners since their Carabao Cup final defeat to Man City.





He missed England’s clashes against Uruguay and Japan during the international break and some Arsenal fans have been concerned he might not play again this season.

But Arteta eased those fears by suggesting the team expect him back in the coming days.

When asked about Saka ahead of their clash against Sporting Lisbon, he replied: “It was something he was carrying a while. It was an achilles issue. There is progression but hopefully days not weeks.”

Arsenal are also concerned about Declan Rice for the Champions League clash after missing team training this week.

Arteta would not explain what happened to the midfielder but said he still had a chance of playing.

He added: “I don’t want to [tell you what’s wrong]. We have to wait and see how he is tomorrow but he was not available to train.

“He has played a lot of games and that is part of the issue but he will try everything he possibly can to be with us.

“We have to wait until tomorrow to see how a few of the boys are and then make the right decision.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Saka and Rice are not Arsenal’s only injury concerns in the build-up to the game.

Jurrien Timber has been out for a month with a groin injury and Arteta said he or Saka had a chance of featuring against Sporting.

Martin Odegaard is also out with a knee injury while Mikel Merino remains sidelined.

Arteta issued a rallying cry to his players ahead of their crucial second leg clash as he urged them to seal a place in the semi-finals.



When asked what he wanted to see from Arsenal, he replied: “Pure fire. From the players and myself. Let’s go for it. I am on fire.

“I have done so much to be in this position. I just see a beautiful opportunity and I want to get it done.

“That is what drives me every day. I have zero fear. This is the biggest opportunity of six and a half years.

“We have the opportunity to go the semi-finals and we could win the Premier League for the first time in 22 years.

“It is difficult and challenging but we are willing to do it. The team is doing something incredible. We have ambition more than anyone else.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola to LEAVE Bournemouth with former Man Utd coach lined up to replace him
Sports.content:
ANDONI IRAOLA will QUIT Bournemouth when his contract expires this summer.

The Cherries had been pushing hard to convince Iraola, 43, to extend his stay on the South Coast.





But following 15 MONTHS of talks, the Spaniard has opted to take the next step in his career nearly three years after first landing in the Premier League.

And Spanish outlet Sport has claimed that his next job will be in LaLiga.

It’s believed he could become the new head coach of Athletic Bilbao following the departure of Ernesto Valverde this summer.

Iraola told the club website: “It has been an honour to manage AFC Bournemouth and I am proud of what we have achieved together.



“I feel this is the right moment for me to step away, but I will always carry fantastic memories of this club.”

Iraola will leave on good terms with Bournemouth chiefs, as reflected in chairman Bill Foley’s statement.

He said: “We are incredibly thankful for his leadership and will always have great memories of our time working together, as well as the things we accomplished.”

Basque-born Iraola has been strongly linked with an emotional return to Athletic Bilbao, where he spent the majority of his playing career and played over 500 games.



Crystal Palace are also believed to be keen as they prepare to lose the outgoing Oliver Glasner.

Bournemouth stars have been informed about Iraola’s decision.

Senior figures at the Vitality Stadium are already in the process of picking out Iraola’s replacement.

According to The Athletic, Ipswich manager Kieran McKenna is high up on their hit list.



McKenna, 39, spent five years at Manchester United, firstly as the Under-18s academy manager and then as a first-team coach.

Sports.title: Fifa trying to use Gianni Infantino’s personal relationship with Donald Trump to halt ICE raids during World Cup
Sports.content:
FIFA are trying to use Gianni Infantino’s personal relationship with Donald Trump to halt anti-immigrant ICE raids during the World Cup.

Zurich bosses have been criticised for Infantino’s decision to get publicly close to the US President.





The Fifa head has been spotted at Trump rallies and the launch of his Peace Board, even wearing a red MAGA cap.

There was a global backlash against Infantino’s push for the establishment of an inaugural Peace Prize that was handed to Trump at the Finals draw in Washington DC in December.

Fifa’s stance has come under even stronger criticism since the start of the US and Israeli military operation against Iran, which has put the attendance of “Team Melli” – due to face Belgium, New Zealand and Egypt in group phase matches in Los Angeles and Seattle – under continuing doubt.

But while there is understood to be some feelings at the highest levels of Fifa that Infantino has got too close to the White House, the Swiss argues that it was imperative to stay on Trump’s good side.

Fifa also felt that Trump’s decision to put the Club World Cup trophy on display in the Oval Office in the build-up to last summer’s tournament added to its success as an event.

And now major Fifa figures have broached the idea of a “moratorium” on the controversial immigration raids during the World Cup which starts in just eight weeks.

ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) operatives have been sent into a number of Democrat controlled “Blue” cities, where opposition to Trump and his policies remains high.

This led to significant clashes which culminated in the deaths of two American citizens protesting against the clampdown in Minneapolis in January.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

After those incidents, the US Homeland Security Department scaled down the operation.

But with European nations having made clear their concerns, the opening of discussions between Fifa and the US Government seems likely to lead to a formal request to Trump from Infantino for the ICE deployment to be put on hold for the duration of the tournament.

While Fifa declined to make any comment, the initial discussions were said to have been around ICE agents being told to stay away from the 11 World Cup venues in the US – in Boston, New York, Atlanta, Philadelphia, Miami, Kansas City, Dallas, Houston, San Francisco as well as the two stadiums where Iran are due to play.

But those talks then widened out with a suggestion that the cities themselves be entirely ICE-free for the duration of the 39-day tournament.

Andrew Giuliani, head of the White House Fifa World Cup Task Force, told The Athletic that Trump has instructed him to “ensure a safe and secure World Cup” with federal and state authorities supporting the host cities.



And while White House spokesperson Davis Ingle declined to respond directly to the reports, he said: “Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, the Fifa World Cup 2026 will be one of the greatest and most spectacular events in the history of mankind, right here in the United States of America.

“This event will generate billions of dollars of economic impact and bring hundreds of thousands of jobs to our country.

“The president is focused on making this the greatest World Cup ever while ensuring it is the safest and most secure in history.”

Sports.content:
Man Utd squad get their way after claiming major decision was 'madness'

A key Manchester United star saw his future resolved with his team-mates clamouring for him to remain at Old Trafford

The Manchester United squad have got their wish after Harry Maguire last week put pen to paper on a one-year extension to his contract. The bulk of the squad believed it would have been "madness" if the experienced defender hadn't been handed a fresh deal.

‌



The 33-year-old is back in favour having endured a tough spell under both Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim. The centre-back, who arrived at United from Leicester City for £80million, has proved to be an influential leader under Michael Carrick's stewardship.

‌



Maguire has led by example for his colleagues and they were reportedly pushing hard for a new contract for the England international. A source told The Sun earlier this year: "The players think it would be madness if he was not offered a new deal.

‌



"Harry has endured plenty of ups and downs at United but has come through all that and is playing really well. He's very well-respected in the dressing room and is passing on a lot of knowledge to some of the younger players like Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro.

"Everyone likes him and respects him and the majority of the players want the club to give him a deal." Reports emerged that AC Milan had been keen on Maguire during the January transfer window.

Sports.title: Tottenham star Richarlison makes startling confession – 'I thought about crashing into a wall'
Sports.content:
Tottenham star Richarlison makes startling confession – 'I thought about crashing into a wall'

Tottenham Hotspur star Richarlison has discussed his mental health struggles

View 2 Images Tottenham Hotspur forward Richarlison has spoken about his battle with depression (Image: Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur star Richarlison has admitted he considered crashing his car into a wall during a battle with depression. The forward was deeply affected by the pressure that surrounded him following Brazil’s exit at the World Cup 2022.

‌



From the outside, the World Cup was a positive experience for the 28-year-old, whose bicycle kick against Serbia won the goal of the tournament. The Spurs forward had been given the honour of leading the line for the five-time World Cup winners.

‌



He scored three goals in total but could not prevent his country from being eliminated by Croatia on penalties in the quarter-finals. However, the disappointment took a toll on his mental health and Richarlison has shared how his thoughts began to spiral.

‌



"One day, while driving, I thought about crashing into a wall,” Richarlison said to France Football. “Today, when I think about it, I tell myself it's pointless.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

He continued: "After the 2022 World Cup, I fell into a depression. Every possible misfortune befell me: the elimination, my agent's betrayal, family problems, physical setbacks... For a year and a half, I suffered blow after blow every single day.”

‌



What every Tottenham star will earn if relegation clauses are triggered - with thousands lost READ MORE :

Premier League relegation picture as Spurs freefall and Leeds hold key with crunch games READ MORE :

Having signed for Spurs from Everton in the summer of 2022, the striker ended his first season with just one league goal. However, through working with a psychologist, Richarlison rediscovered a more positive mindset.

"It was the first time I had to deal with so many problems,” he explained. ”In all that chaos, I met an honest lawyer who put my affairs and assets in order. I worked with a psychologist and, most importantly, I met my wife."

As the World Cup 2026 approaches, the former Everton icon plans to take Manchester United midfielder Casemiro’s advice and not look at social media if he is named in Carlo Ancelotti’s squad. However, it is not the first time that Richarlison has given an insight into his struggles with depression.

‌



View 2 Images Richarlison struggled after Brazil were knocked out of the 2022 World Cup (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

In March 2024, during a heartfelt interview with ESPN Brasil, the Spurs striker said: “I was reaching my limit, you know? I don’t know, I’m not going to talk about killing myself, but I was in a depression there, and I wanted to give up.”

He added: “Today I can say, look for a psychologist, if you need a psychologist, look for one because it’s nice for you to open up like that, for you to be talking to the person.

‌



“Today a (psychologist) came to thank me for taking this to the world of football, to the world, outside the pitch too, because it is very important and, whether we like it or not, it saves lives.

“I had this prejudice before, I thought it was nonsense, I thought I was crazy. In my family, there are people who think that anyone who goes to a psychologist thinks they are crazy, they think they are insane. But I discovered this and thought it was wonderful. The best thing, really the best discovery I’ve ever had in my life.”

Richarlison has scored 10 goals in 38 appearances for Spurs this season. He most recently played for Brazil in October 2025.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has made his first serious error in audition for Man Utd job
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has made his first serious error in audition for Man Utd job

On-trial Manchester United manager was furious with referee Paul Tierney after the defeat to Leeds United at Old Trafford but he should have been blaming others closer to home

View 2 Images Michael Carrick came out with highly critical comments about the refereeing of his side's loss to Leeds United (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

Without doubt, the Lisandro Martinez hair-pull was even less violent than the one which got Everton’s Michael Keane sent off against Wolves at Hill Dickinson Stadium back in January. But from the moment Keane’s ‘offence’ against Wolves’ Tolu Arokodare was deemed worthy of a straight red card - and a three-match suspension - it was clear Premier League referees had been given the word.

‌



Zero tolerance on hair-pulling. A yank, a tug, whatever, it doesn’t matter. And no matter how incredulous Michael Carrick and a legion of ex-professionals declared themselves to be, there will be no change in the policy. Certainly not this season.

‌



Pull hair, get sent off. And no matter how soft the dismissal of Martinez looked, you cannot accidentally pull someone’s hair.

‌



Whether this zero-tolerance approach will continue next season is another matter, but the problem referees will have is deciding when a hair-pull is soft enough for a yellow card or no punishment, and when it is hard enough for a red card. Far simpler to say: hey, just don’t pull someone’s hair.

Anyway, the point is that while the red card for Martinez did seem extremely harsh, it was not ‘absolutely shocking’. Once Paul Tierney believes the footage shows even the slightest pull, the Manchester United man is off.

Andoni Iraola to leave Bournemouth as Man Utd learn chances of landing new boss READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



What was shocking, though, was Carrick’s post-match reaction. It was his first serious mis-step in his extended audition for the long-term job.

That he was outraged by the decision was not shocking - a lot of people were equally outraged. I can safely say in the list of Martinez offences that have been deemed worthy of sanction since he has been in the Premier League, this was way down the scale.

But Carrick had just enjoyed the luxury of three weeks to prepare for a game against a team that had won just ONE Premier League away game all season. And that win was against a Wolves team at their most hapless early in the season.

‌



And don’t forget, Carrick has a squad assembled at a cost in excess of £800 million. The total outlay on Daniel Farke’s squad was just over £200million. Most pertinently of all, Leeds United were two goals to the good at the time of the Martinez offence and looked in relatively little danger.

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez was stunned by Paul Tierney's decision to send him off for a hair-pull on Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Image: Getty Images)

You can easily understand the manager’s frustration. He is now going to be without Martinez for three games, although even before the red card, it would be fair to describe the Argentine’s comeback performance as mixed.

‌



But even if it was not his intention, Carrick’s broadside against the officials diverted attention away from the most unsatisfactory performance in what is essentially a trial period for the manager, and the message from Carrick should have been clear. He didn’t agree with the sending-off call but the real issue is that United players had lapsed into pre-Carrick levels of performance and that is something he will address.

Heading into the remaining six Premier League fixtures with a seven-point advantage over sixth-placed Chelsea (the top five qualify for the Champions League), Carrick is still in the box seat for the long-term role. But Monday night’s efforts - and the subsequent moaning about officials - were the sorts of things that could change executive opinion of Carrick very dramatically.

Sports.title: Gary Neville identifies Man Utd detail that gives biggest hint yet over manager decision
Sports.content:
Gary Neville identifies Man Utd detail that gives biggest hint yet over manager decision

Former Manchester United captain Gary Neville has spotted something which could signify where the club are headed in their pursuit of a new permanent manager

View 3 Images Gary Neville has offered insight into Manchester United's plans (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Manchester United are yet to officially confirm who they plan to install as their next permanent manager. However, former captain Gary Neville thinks he has spotted indicators the club are preparing Michael Carrick to remain part of the picture at Old Trafford next season.

‌



Carrick has done a commendable job since stepping in after Ruben Amorim was sacked in January. A haul of 23 points from 11 fixtures leaves United third in the table and gives them a solid chance of returning to the Champions League, though they will need to bounce back after losing at home to Leeds United on Monday.

‌



Speaking prior to that fixture, Neville and his former Old Trafford colleague Roy Keane discussed Carrick's future. Both men anticipated the interim boss would land the job on a permanent basis and Neville backed that up with a revealing observation.

‌



"It was interesting in his press conference. He was asked about whether he was part of recruitment meetings and planning for next season and Michael said yes he was," said Neville, who suggested the stability offered by the interim boss could help him land the job permanently.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Latest Man Utd injury news before Chelsea clash as Kobbie Mainoo 'issue' confirmed READ MORE :

"What Michael's doing right now, not just winning football matches which is critical, he's settling the club down off the pitch as well which will be important," he added. "If you're an owner and the rest of the club trust the manager, like the manager and feel he has a good way about him, that will count as they move towards the end of the season."

‌



Carrick's involvement in forward-planning could well be telling. Were United to appoint a new manager currently in post elsewhere, there would be considerably less time to finalise plans regarding recruitment, tactics and beyond.

It is also worth bearing in mind that several international managers who might have been in contention following the World Cup have since penned extensions with their respective national sides. Carlo Ancelotti has agreed fresh terms with Brazil, while Thomas Tuchel's England contract has been extended until 2028.

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel was linked with United before extending his England contract (Image: Michael Regan - The FA, The FA via Getty Images)

‌



With six league fixtures remaining, Carrick and United enjoy a seven-point cushion above sixth-place Chelsea. The top five Premier League finishers will secure their place in next season's Champions League but the job is far from done.

United face Chelsea next week in a fixture that could prove decisive for both clubs' European aspirations. Both sides head into the match on the back of defeats, with the Blues falling to Manchester City on Sunday and Carrick's men coming unstuck against Leeds.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick could yet get the United job permanently (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



A brace from Noah Okafor in the first half put the visitors firmly in control at Old Trafford on Monday, before Lisandro Martinez was shown a red card for a hair pull. Casemiro pulled one back for United but they couldn't grab a crucial second goal.

"I have to say, whatever happened tonight, it's not going to suddenly change my opinion on what we are as a team," Carrick said following Monday's defeat. "We've built enough of a foundation to kind of understand what we're good at and what we need to improve on.

"Moving forward at the end of the season, the games are going to be the games and it's a big end of the season. There's no getting away from it. The kind of mentality and the character of the boys wanting to do well and trying to give everything, I've never doubted that, and I won't doubt that."

Sports.title: Dominik Szoboszlai agrees with Arne Slot on how Liverpool must replace Mo Salah
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai agrees with Arne Slot on how Liverpool must replace Mo Salah

Liverpool will wave goodbye to Mohamed Salah after nine years and many goals this summer and discussions have already been held internally about how they can replace him

View 2 Images Dominik Szoboszlai has spoken about life at Liverpool without Mohamed Salah (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

Dominik Szoboszlai has backed up Arne Slot's assertion that responsibility should fall upon last summer's big-money signings to replace Mohamed Salah at Liverpool next season. Liverpool are preparing for life without Salah after the 33-year-old announced he would leave the club at the end of the campaign.

‌



Salah has 256 goals and 122 assists in 437 games for Liverpool and, even though his performances have dipped this season, he has still contributed 11 goals and nine assists in 36 games across all competitions. Liverpool have struggled in attack at times this season, with fitness issues and a lack of consistency undermining their performances.

‌



Alexander Isak was the headline £125million signing in the summer but has barely featured, while fellow new arrivals Hugo Ekitike and Florian Wirtz are yet to consistently hit the heights Liverpool expected. Szoboszlai says that, having had a season to bed in, the attacking trio must step up to the plate once Salah has left next season.

‌



“I can mention Mo, last season he won the Premier League for us, with his numbers," Szoboszlai told Prime Video ahead of Liverpool's second leg against Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday night. "Maybe he’s not at this level right now, which he knows. Maybe people were expecting more from the (new) guys who came in.

"But to come to the Premier League is not that easy. I can’t remember a player who came to the Premier League directly and didn’t show any setbacks. We need to give them time, to give them confidence, and trust me, if they have time and confidence, they will be needed in the future of Liverpool."

‌



The Liverpool midfielder's words echo those of his manager, who addressed the "impossible" task of replacing Salah earlier in the month. "Of course we do," Slot said earlier in April when asked if Liverpool had a plan for replacing Salah.

View 2 Images Arne Slot has to replace Mohamed Salah (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"We are not starting to work on it now because we are constantly working on where we can improve. There is not a lot talked about this but it is 88 minutes that Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Florian Wirtz were together on the pitch together.

‌



"So let’s first find out and work out how that works together and that can give us so much more. It is never one player who can replace Mo. Otherwise there would be 15 or 20 Mo’s and he is one of a kind, which is why he is so special. You cannot find a Mo replacement. Maybe you can but he would not be available."

He added: replacing Mo on a one-on-one is probably impossible. So we have to find a way of making it work that the team is stronger but it would already make our team much stronger if we've got Alex, Hugo and Florian together available for a bit more than 88 minutes this year."

Bournemouth have been unsuccessful in their attempts to keep hold of highly-rated head coach Andoni Iraola, who will now be in demand across Europe this summer

Manchester United will face a tough task in trying to tempt Andoni Iraola to become their next long-term manager this summer, even though he is poised to leave Bournemouth at the end of the season.

"I’m thankful to the players and staff that I’ve worked with, as well as [chairman] Bill (Foley), who have all made my time here so special. As for the fans, you have continued to show your fantastic support to myself and the team, and for that I will always be grateful. I feel this is the right moment for me to step away, but I will always carry fantastic memories of this club.”

‌



After leading the Cherries to ninth and 12-place finishes in his first two seasons, he has them 11th and unbeaten in 12 games following their stunning 2-1 win over Arsenal on Saturday. But despite his reputation being sky-high in the Premier League, Iraola appears to have his heart set on a return to Spain. BBC Sport reports that the 43-year-old is keen to return to his home country with his family, with a move to Athletic Club appearing the most likely option.

Iraola spent 12 years playing for the team as a player and has a strong connection with the Basque club, where he made over 400 appearances. He is considered a legend at Athletic Club, who are 11th in La Liga, and United are very unlikely to be able to compete.

United have Michael Carrick as interim manager until the end of the season but are still to confirm their long-term successor to Ruben Amorim, who was sacked in January. Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada have been content to move slowly in making the decision, with United sat third in the Premier League and on course to qualify for the Champions League.

‌



View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is in high demand (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

“Andoni has been instrumental in shaping the direction of this football club over the past three seasons," Bournemouth chairman Foley said. "He brought intensity, innovation, and a clear philosophy that elevated AFC Bournemouth both on and off the pitch. We are incredibly thankful for his leadership and will always have great memories of our time working together, as well as the things we accomplished.”

Bournemouth were understood to have been trying to strike an agreement over a new deal for the past 15 months but the Spaniard is set for a new spell of his career. Bournemouth have six games remaining this season, starting with a trip to Newcastle on Saturday.

Sports.title: Man Utd debate put to bed by PGMOL rule and Howard Webb after red card fury
Sports.content:
Man Utd debate put to bed by PGMOL rule and Howard Webb after red card fury

Lisandro Martinez was shown a red card for pulling the hair of Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the second half as Leeds United beat Manchester United

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez was sent off for pulling Dominic Calvert-Lewin's hair (Image: Sky Sports)

Tuesday morning saw widespread discussion about Lisandro Martinez's red card for pulling Dominic Calvert-Lewin's hair during the second half of Leeds United's victory over Manchester United.

‌



The Red Devils defender was dismissed 11 minutes into the second period for grabbing Calvert-Lewin's hair, with VAR recommending the sending-off after summoning referee Paul Tierney to the pitchside monitor.

‌



Momentum surprisingly shifted towards the visitors afterwards, with Casemiro reducing the deficit to set up a tense final 20 minutes for Leeds with his header. He came agonisingly close to snatching an 86th-minute leveller but for Calvert-Lewin's goal-line clearance, while Karl Darlow made several outstanding stops.

‌



Latest Man Utd injury news before Chelsea clash as Kobbie Mainoo 'issue' confirmed READ MORE :

Sky Sports fail to apologise after X-rated outburst as Man Utd shocked by Leeds READ MORE :

Man United interim manager Michael Carrick believed Calvert-Lewin should have been punished for an arm on Leny Yoro in the lead-up to Noah Okafor's opening goal, before questioning Martinez's subsequent red card.

"The arm [is] in the face of Lisandro and he is off balance and grappling. He goes to touch his shirt and gets a red card for it. It is not aggressive, there is no jolt, no tug. We have got to be careful where the game is going. It is a shocking decision, absolutely shocking. The red card, that is really concerning.

"I know he touched his hair. There is a difference to really aggressively touching it."

‌



View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez was sent off for pulling Dominic Calvert-Lewin's hair

The word 'aggression' doesn't actually appear in guidance issued to Premier League officials by refereeing body PGMOL, but instead 'force'. On page 96 of the 2025/26 PGMO Premier League handbook guide, it reads that violent conduct includes "clearly pulling the hair of an opponent with force".

Calvert-Lewin appealed to the official about the hair pull, with his bobble coming loose as Martinez grabbed his hair.

‌



PGMOL boss Howard Webb clarified the rule guidance in greater detail when Everton's Michael Keane was handed a red card for pulling the hair of Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare in January.

"For some years now, actions where players pull opponents' hair have been deemed as violent conduct," he said. "You don't see that often, you sometimes see it with players maybe in confrontation with one another, not battling for the ball.

"I'm told if you have your hair pulled, it's quite an offensive thing to happen to you - I've not had mine pulled for a long time – but I think we've recognised that and it is in the guidance that we give to clubs before the season starts.

Article continues below

"Grabbing somebody's hair with force is deemed violent conduct and a player will be sent off. It was the appropriate outcome. It was unusual but if we see it again next week, it will be the same outcome next week as well."

Therefore, according to the guidance and regulations, it was accurate to issue Martinez the red card. Whether the rule requires more precise definition is a separate discussion altogether.

Sports.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Hoping to learn more about Derby hope Wareeth
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle is in action at Newmarket's Craven meeting this week, including an exciting ride on Derby hopeful Wareeth in the Listed Feilden Stakes.

We'll find out if we have a potential Derby horse on Wednesday when my boss Archie Watson's exciting colt WAREETH - my stand-out ride at this week's Craven Meeting at Newmarket - takes his chance in the Listed Feilden Stakes (2.25).

The extra furlong will be ideal for the son of Sea The Stars, who takes a big step up in class after winning his novice over 1m at Newcastle last month by a commanding 14 lengths.

Though he doesn't hold a Derby entry, we've been delighted with Sheikh Ahmed Al Maktoum's colt since that racecourse debut. He felt good when I sat on him last week, but we'll know a lot more after this second start.

Aidan O'Brien's Isaac Newton certainly has an edge of experience having won his maiden at Goodwood before finishing a promising fourth in the Group 1 Criterium de Saint-Cloud in the autumn. He does hold a Derby entry and sets the standard with an official rating of 106.

Like Wareeth, Godolphin's colt Poseidon's Warrior makes the leap from novice company after winning over this distance at Goodwood and is also in the Classic. Unsurprisingly, all three colts are entered in the traditional Derby trial, the Group 2 Dante at York next month.

Zoulu can repeat Autumn track form

Heather Main's sprinter ZOULU CHIEF ran a lovely race for me at Newmarket back in the autumn so I'm expecting another big run from him in the Weatherbys With Venatour Racing Handicap (1.50) on Wednesday.

He's been busy on the All-Weather over the winter, winning around Wolverhampton before giving subsequent Listed dead-heater Completely Random a good battle at Lingfield Park.

Approaching his prime as a five-year-old, he's a few pounds higher than his best winning performance at York in 2023 but looks every bit a 90 horse.

Image: Zoulu Chief in winning action at Newbury

Harlequin worth her place in Nell Gwyn

I've ridden work on Jane Chapple-Hyam's outsider HARLEQUIN BREEZE and can tell you she is certainly worth her place in the Group 3 Lanwades Stud Nell Gwyn Stakes (3.35) on Wednesday.

Despite her likely odds, this tough daughter of New Bay brings some potentially smart form into this Betfred 1000 Guineas trial after getting within a neck of William Haggas's well-regarded Zooming, who is set to re-appear in the Fred Darling at Newbury on Saturday.

Harlequin Breeze is still a maiden after three starts but has improved with every run and impressed me with her determination over course and distance back in November.

Mission not impossible for Butler colt

IMPOSSIBLE MISSION needs to prove he's at least as good on turf as he is on the All-Weather when he receives weight from all his rivals in the National Stud Handicap (5.17) on Wednesday.

John Butler's three-year-old made a winning handicap debut under Neil Callan at Wolverhampton in November and should have come on for his reappearance there last month when he was just too keen.

Meanwhile, it will be all about experience for Des Donovan's LADY FIZZ in the Molson Coors British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (4.45). This debutant takes on fillies from some powerful yards over 1m which may be a minimum trip for her in due course, being out of a 10f winning daughter of Golden Horn.

Prince should be spot on for Abernant

I'm looking forward to being back at Newmarket on Thursday to ride Marco Botti's Shergar Cup winner PRINCE OF INDIA in the Zyn Abernant Stakes (3.00).

It'll be the first time I've ridden him on the track but I liked him when I sat on him on the gallops last year. He's a powerfully built colt who could prove a force in stakes sprints this summer.

It looks like being a wide-open race but this son of Wootton Bassett should be spot on after a creditable comeback in the Listed Lady Wulfruna Stakes at Wolverhampton last month.

Mountain sets demanding standard in Craven

I'm expecting big things from Hawk Mountain this year, so I'll be disappointed if he doesn't make a winning return in the Group 3 Betway Craven Stakes (3.35) at Newmarket on Thursday.

Aidan O'Brien's son of Wootton Bassett is already a Group 1 winner after taking the Futurity Trophy at Doncaster last October and can strengthen his own Derby claims at Headquarter.

Another favourite of mine is Karl Burke's Boiling Point who returns to turf in the Group 3 Betway Earl Of Sefton Stakes (3.00) on Wednesday. The Cambridgeshire winner probably needed the outing in a steadily run Winter Derby but with that run under his girth can establish himself as a genuine Pattern performer this season.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: How long can India ignore Sooryavanshi - and could he be unleashed on England?
Sports.content:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi wrote his name into the history books by becoming the youngest‑ever IPL centurion - just nine days after his record‑breaking debut as a 14‑year‑old in 2025.

Now 15, India's latest cricketing prodigy has continued his remarkable trajectory, fuelling calls for him to be unleashed on the international stage.

Sooryavanshi lit up his debut IPL season with a 35‑ball hundred as a 14‑year‑old, and he has proven to be anything but a flash in the pan in the 2026 edition, showcasing a staggering ability to thrive on the biggest stages with the Rajasthan Royals.

He has already registered two 15‑ball fifties - against Chennai Super Kings and Royal Challengers Bengaluru - and is the third‑highest run‑scorer in the tournament, with 200 runs from five innings at a strike rate of 263.15.

A golden duck in Monday's defeat to Sunrisers Hyderabad proved Sooryavanshi was human, but with ball‑striking power, physical presence and crease composure far beyond his age, he has seasoned professionals watching in awe.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 15-year-old sensation Sooryavanshi falls for a golden duck as Rajasthan Royals crash to four wickets in the first ten balls of a nightmare start!

'Cricket is not as easy as he's playing'

"We just cannot believe how someone can hit like that. He is a great talent and we feel good that he is in our team," said India and Rajasthan Royals wicketkeeper‑batter Dhruv Jurel.

"When you go in, and Vaibhav is smashing every ball, you tend to think nothing is happening on the wicket. Cricket is not as easy as he's playing."

With would‑be international team‑mates like Jurel waxing lyrical about his ability, it begs one pertinent question.

How long can India ignore Sooryavanshi?

India have an embarrassment of riches when it comes to emerging talent, and with their T20 side newly-crowned World Cup winners, it remains to be seen whether selectors see fit to tinker with a winning formula.

But every now and then a player so special arrives that they simply cannot be ignored.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player When he was 14, Sooryavanshi smashed 175 off just 80 balls as India dominated England in the Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup final

Sachin Tendulkar. Virat Kohli. Rohit Sharma. Shubman Gill. Yashasvi Jaiswal. Sooryavanshi appears to be cut from that cloth.

A sensational 175 fired India to a 100-run victory over England - and a record sixth title - in February's U19 World Cup final in Harare, as he once again proved he cut it against the very best.

Sooryavanshi bow on British Isles?

A stacked summer of white‑ball fixtures presents ample opportunity for him to make his international bow.

If calls to hand the 15‑year‑old a debut in the upcoming multi‑format series against Afghanistan go unanswered, his breakthrough could come in the British Isles, with India facing Ireland and England across seven T20Is and three ODIs in June and July.

Whether it comes this summer or not, it seems only a matter of time before Sooryavanshi gets the call from India. The world of cricket has been put on notice.

Sports.title: 'I'm on fire!' - Arteta calls for 'no fear' in his biggest week at Arsenal
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has called for Arsenal to have "no fear" and "pure fire" in an extraordinary rallying cry ahead of the biggest week of his career at the club.

Arsenal are attempting to reach back-to-back Champions League semi-finals for the first time in the club's history, with a potential Premier League title decider at Manchester City, live on Sky Sports, waiting in the wings on Sunday.

But Arsenal go into this week on a run of three defeats in four matches, going from four possible trophies to two. And after a shock home defeat by Bournemouth, Arteta's ability to keep his team calm in the most important part of the season has been questioned.

But Arteta was at it again in the press conference room by admitting he himself is on "fire" ahead of the Champions League quarter-final second leg with Sporting CP on Wednesday, with his team 1-0 up on aggregate.

Asked what he wants from his team on Wednesday night, Arteta took his time for a few seconds and then replied: "No fear. Pure fire. That's it.

"That's what I want to see from the players, the people and myself. Go for every opportunity. It's unbelievable.

"We are in April, an incredible opportunity ahead of us. Let's confront it and go for it. I am putting everything into it.

"Fire! I'm on fire! That's it. Nothing else. I'm dreaming so much.

Image: Mikel Arteta admits he is on fire right now

"I've done so much to be in this position. Because I know how this club was. I've done so much against anything that I just see beauty, opportunity. I want to get it done who have been on this journey with us. They deserve it, it's unbelievable.

"I have zero fear. I had fear when: if we don't get this done, I don't know what happens to the club. Now? It's just purpose, fire, direction."

Asked if he is seeing it in his players, Arteta replied: "Yes. Big time."

And asked if this is the biggest week of his Arsenal career, Arteta replied: "The biggest opportunity of six and a half years, yeah."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz looks at the influence Manchester City's Carabao Cup final win has had over Arsenal and whether it has revealed a blueprint in how to beat the Gunners.

Arteta reacts to Man City fan 'bottle' moment

Arsenal have been accused of "bottling" the Premier League title race, as they missed the chance to go 12 points clear of Manchester City on Saturday, before Pep Guardiola's side - who have a game in hand - cut their lead to six by beating Chelsea on Sunday.

One Manchester City fan drank from an Arsenal 'bottle' in the away end - a clip which ended up going viral - and Arteta responded to that moment.

"One fan?" Arteta replied. "One fan that says something, over 60,000 fans that are incredible at the Emirates? I don't get moved by that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Man City fan pretends to drink from an Arsenal water bottle after Man City go 3-0 up against Chelsea.

"I show [my players] all the people and players that love these players for what they're doing which is unprecedented in this club."

"What we are trying to achieve, it's difficult, challenging, bumpy at times. It's supposed to be like this. You have to confront it."

Arteta defended Arsenal's recent wobble in form - admitting that getting over the line to claim a first Premier League title in 22 years, and reaching the latter stages of the Champions League is meant to be difficult.

"We are trying to do something, in this competition, that hasn't been done in the history of the club - in 140 years," said the Arsenal manager. "That tells you the difficulty of that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville suggests Mikel Arteta and his team need to normalise their preparation as much as possible ahead of their massive title run-in match against rivals Manchester City.

"We value a lot where we are. We want to be in the semi-finals. We are in a really strong position in the Premier League for 22 years without doing it. So we know the difficulty of that. The beauty of it, is that it's difficult.

"We haven't been in this position in the Champions League ever in our history. We have overcome a lot of hurdles that were there for 140 years, they've never been done before.

"If we want to go to the next step, for sure, we have to have more ambition than anyone else. We are doing it, and are very, very close.

"What I love about where we are is that there is no satisfaction about it. You haven't asked me any questions about: congratulations, you're going to be in the Champions League next year.

"Now we take it for granted. I assume the next 20 years this club is going to take it for granted that you're fighting for titles in April. C'est finit. That's great. I do value a lot what the players have done."

Is Arteta doing the right thing by calling for fire?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

After last week's stunning 'bring your lunch, bring your dinner' rallying cry to his supporters, only for his side to lose to Bournemouth, Mikel Arteta could have opted for a quieter approach this press conference.

Many felt Arteta's antics last week added more to the noise, the expectation and the pressure of the team - and it led to a jittery display at the weekend.

And anyway, his team are 1-0 up in the Champions League quarter-final tie, they are expected to progress to the European semi-finals - and Wednesday's encounter with Sporting CP is not even Arsenal's biggest game of the week.

But the Arsenal manager has doubled down - producing yet another rallying cry. Instead of calling for calm, or producing the usual 'one game at a time line', he has stolen the headlines once again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tim Sherwood and Sam Blitz are on Fan Club on Sky Sports News to take a closer look at why Arsenal's nervous mentality could be a key factor in whether they win the Premier League title or not.

At the start of the season, many observers of Arteta noticed a much calmer version of the Spaniard. That calm came from the confidence he had in his team: a bigger squad, better chances of success - and it exuded confidence in his players.

Now this version of Arteta is very, very different. And it is a complete contrast to the Manchester City camp, which is cool, composed and controlled by Pep Guardiola.

The Arsenal manager has drawn the line in the sand: his Arsenal team are showing a burning desire for success. But is this latest speech going to fire up his players - or send his season up in smoke?

Eze: You can see the fire in Arteta's eyes

Speaking before the quarter-final, Arsenal midfielder Eberechi Eze says Arteta has "fire" in his eyes - and that the squad are keen to ignore the noise about their season.

"The boss speaks well, he is passionate, and you can see the fire he has in his eyes and mind, and that has been pushed around the whole training ground," he said.

"We know the opportunity we have, we know what is at stake and what is possible, but we have an opportunity to make history as a club.

"And regardless of what people are saying outside, it is about us here and what we do massively, we have so much confidence in what we are doing and that has been the main message - just focus on what we are doing and this feeling we have and letting go of all the noise outside."

Eze could be crucial in overcoming Arsenal's recent attacking woes and is eyeing up a first start since getting injured in the Champions League last 16 win over Bayer Leverkusen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson reacts to SENSATIONAL Eberechi Eze opener for Arsenal against Bayer Leverkusen.

Asked if he has been tested at Arsenal, Eze said: "I would not say tested. I've experienced football for long enough to know how to carry myself and operate and be the best version of myself on the pitch.

"And a lot of that is, to be honest, not caring what you guys talk about and just doing what I do. I am professional and the one who plays and everyone has an opinion and thinks they know what is right.

"And I can see we now have the mentality just to let go and do what we do best."

Sports.title: Tomkins departs Catalans Dragons due to 'personal reasons'
Sports.content:
Joel Tomkins has confirmed he has chosen to step down from his role as head coach at Catalans Dragons, a role he held for just under a year, due to "personal reasons".

The former England rugby league and union international revealed that time away from family had been challenging and after a recent period of time back at home, he made the decision to leave Dragons after seven games of the Super League season with the side sixth in the table.

Initially Tomkins had taken on the role as an interim coach following Steve McNamara's departure, but within months he was appointed to the permanent role at the club he had spent the last years of his playing career at.

"My time at Catalans Dragons over the past 18 months has brought plenty of highs, along with some challenges, all of which I've genuinely valued as a rookie head coach," Tomkins said.

"I've learned a great deal, both personally and professionally, and I'm grateful for the friendships and experiences I've gained along the way.

"I leave the club a better coach than when I arrived.

"However, living away from my family for a prolonged period has been difficult.

"After recently spending some time back at home due to personal reasons, I've taken the decision to step away and bring my time at the club to a close.

"I'm very grateful to the players, staff and supporters, and I wish the club every success for the remainder of the season and in future."

Tomkins had been absent from the club's last three fixtures, in which they took one win after winning three of their first four, sparking belief that the former Wigan Warriors star would be making an exit.

Sports.title: Iraola to leave Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Bournemouth head coach Andoni Iraola is leaving at the end of the season.

The Bournemouth head coach is out of contract in three months and has turned down numerous offers to extend his stay amid interest from his former club Athletic Club and links to Premier League rivals.

Iraola, who has six games left at Bournemouth, departs after a record-breaking three years on the south coast. He said "this is the right moment for me to step away" in a statement on the club's website.

The Spaniard's final home game is against Manchester City on Sunday May 17, ahead of a trip to Nottingham Forest on the last day of the Premier League season.

Bournemouth felt they tried everything possible to persuade Iraola to stay, and although they are disappointed with his decision, there remains a mutual respect between the two parties.

Talks were first opened over 15 months ago, but Iraola preferred to wait until later in the campaign to have those meaningful conversations.

The search for a new head coach had been taking place in the background for some time, and Sky Sports News understands there are three favoured candidates on Bournemouth's shortlist.

Bournemouth, currently 11th, could end Iraola's time on a high with a first European qualification in the club's history still a possibility this season.

They sit two points adrift of seventh, which would be enough to play in the Conference League next season.

Iraola has been a popular figure at Bournemouth since he was appointed in June 2023 to replace Gary O'Neil, implementing an attacking, progressive and dynamic style of football.

Bournemouth finished ninth in the Premier League table last season, finishing with a club-record 56 points, breaking the Cherries' best top-flight return for a second season running.

Iraola has had to cope with the sales of Dean Huijsen, Milos Kerkez, Illia Zabarnyi, Dango Ouattara and Antoine Semenyo this season for £253m.

Where could Iraola go next?

Image: Iraola is set to move on this summer - but where will he go?

Iraola will depart Bournemouth as one of the Premier League's hottest coaching prospects – but where could he be off to next?

Athletic Club are interested in bringing Iraola back to the Basque Country as they search for a new head coach with Ernesto Valverde set to depart at the end of the season.

Iraola spent 12 years in Bilbao and played more than 500 games for the club. He was captain of the Marcelo Bielsa side that knocked Sir Alex Ferguson's Manchester United out of the Europa League in 2011/12.

Sky in Germany understands former Borussia Dortmund boss Edin Terzic is another potential candidate for Athletic Club - but any decision is expected to have to wait for the outcome of the club's presidential elections in May.

Crystal Palace viewed Iraola as a prime candidate to replace the departing Oliver Glasner but are believed to have moved on to other targets. Before Iraola decided on his Bournemouth future, it was thought to be unlikely that he would make the switch to Selhurst Park.

Tottenham were among the clubs linked with Iraola but have now appointed Roberto De Zerbi on a five-year contract.

Manchester United are yet to make a final decision on who their next head coach will be for next season with Michael Carrick in post until the summer. United have not spoken to any other candidates at this stage and will not rush into an appointment.

Speculation around Eddie Howe's future at Newcastle has seen Iraola shorten in the odds to become the favourite with some bookies to be the next to take over at St James' Park.

Howe said last week that he is 100 per cent committed to Newcastle but that it is "very difficult" to look too far beyond this season.
